Shell Insider Sale Lands Alongside LBBW's Target Hike and a Fresh LNG Offtake
sum: A seven-figure share disposal by one of Shell's senior trading executives surfaced on Monday, the same day the energy major's LNG arm put pen to paper on a five-year supply deal with Greece's METLEN. Andrew Smith, president of Trading and Supply, offloaded 33,000 ordinary shares on 30 October for a reported total of €1,604,528.15, according to a regulatory disclosure.

The sale is a routine notification and carries no read-through on the company's outlook. Far more consequential for the equity story was LBBW's move on Wednesday, when the Landesbank reportedly lifted its price target on Shell from 3,600 to 4,300 pence while keeping its buy rating intact — a change in the target mark, not in the recommendation itself.

The upgrade follows third-quarter 2026 results published on 29 October, when Shell posted adjusted earnings of $10.814 billion. Management credited strong operational performance and record-high refining margins for the result. Cash flow from operations came in at $21.043 billion, with free cash flow reaching $16.322 billion.
Shareholders were handed an interim dividend of US$0.3906 per ordinary share. The stock goes ex-dividend on 12 November, with a record date of 13 November and payment scheduled for 21 December.

Capital returns extend beyond the dividend. Roughly a week before the results, Shell kicked off a $5 billion share buyback running for about three months, with repurchased stock set to be cancelled. The programme permits purchases of up to 470,000,000 ordinary shares — a ceiling written into the terms, not a tally of what has already been bought.

On the commercial front, Shell Trading Rotterdam on Monday signed a long-term offtake agreement with Green Sky Manara covering output from a planned plant at Port Nador in Morocco. The contract grants exclusive rights to roughly 150,000 tonnes per year of sustainable aviation fuel, or an equivalent volume of hydrotreated vegetable oil, alongside bionaphtha and biopropane. The facility is slated to start operations in October 2028.
The METLEN deal, announced by the Greek group, adds six LNG cargoes a year over five years beginning in 2027, with Shell Global LNG Limited as the counterparty.

sum: The Sakhalin Papers XCIX: The Shareholding That Survived — Shell’s Bermuda Company, Its Russian LNG Contracts and the Exit That Remained Incomplete

Researched and drafted with assistance from ChatGPT, using authenticated Shell financial statements, original corporate announcements, SEC filings, contemporaneous reporting, historical documents preserved in the Donovan–Shell Archive and publicly accessible regulatory records.

Nearly five years after Shell announced its intention to withdraw from its Russian energy investments, the company’s own financial disclosures reveal a complicated legal inheritance. Shell still reported ownership of 27.5% minus one share in the original Bermuda-registered company that once operated Sakhalin II, even though Russia had transferred the project’s operating rights to a replacement company. One long-term Russian LNG purchase agreement had been declared terminated following non-performance. Another, signed with a Novatek subsidiary in 2015, remained listed in Shell’s 2025 annual report. These are not indications that Shell secretly continued operating Sakhalin II. They demonstrate something more technically significant: withdrawing from an investment, losing control of its operating assets, terminating associated contracts and extinguishing every residual corporate right are different legal and financial events. The authenticated records allow those distinctions to be reconstructed.
Previous instalment: SLF-2007-108 — The Account That Could Not Pay, 4 November 2026

Principal authenticated evidence: Shell’s announcements of 28 February and 8 March 2022; Shell’s 2022, 2023 and 2025 Forms 20-F; Shell’s third-quarter 2026 interim financial report; the original 2015 Novatek LNG contract announcement; Shell’s April 2007 SEC-filed Sakhalin announcement; and contemporaneous Interfax, Reuters and S&P Global reporting.

Evidence standard: Corporate ownership is distinguished from operational participation; accounting carrying value from legal title; the existence of a contract from physical delivery under that contract; and the assertions of parties in a legal dispute from independently established judicial findings.

Shell And 2 Other British Undervalued Stocks To Watch
sum: UK interest rates look set for a fresh rise as the Bank of England pushes back against stubborn inflation, which keeps pressure on borrowing costs and squeezes highly valued shares. That backdrop can leave some cash rich British businesses trading for less than the cash they are expected to generate. This article highlights three such UK stocks that screen as attractively priced on future cash flows.

The three stocks covered below are only a sample, since the full screen also surfaced 21 more businesses that look just as interesting on their cash flow narratives but are not covered in this article. To identify and analyze the wider opportunity set, head straight to the Undervalued Stocks Based On Cash Flows screener.

Shell is a global energy group that still earns most of its money from traditional oil, gas and chemicals, yet is steadily building a Renewables and Energy Solutions arm linked to low carbon fuels, EV charging and carbon capture, and carries a market value of about £216.4b.

For a cash flow focused investor, Shell matters because it mixes a large, established hydrocarbon engine with growing transition projects that could reshape how its future earnings are valued. That mix is exactly the tension this screener is trying to surface.

With an LNG portfolio exceeding 60 million tons and significant trading capabilities, Shell is often viewed as a company that can be sensitive to volatility in the global gas market. Some market commentators note that factors such as economic growth in Asia and energy security considerations in Europe are expected by various industry forecasts to contribute to higher LNG demand by 2040.
What happens to that LNG and trading profit pool if a single pressure point quietly shifts the balance between tight supply and long term contracts?
When that balance shifts, the full narrative for Shell shows how Shell's cash engine and transition bets could be accelerating, or quietly masking, future value.

Shell (LSE:SHEL) Could Be 11% Undervalued After Q3 Earnings And Dividend
Shell stock enters stronger capital-return phase after Q3 beat
sum: Shell reported a strong third quarter on October 29, 2026, with adjusted earnings of 10.8 billion US dollars and operating cash flow of 21 billion US dollars. The figures were presented on Shell's official quarterly results page.

Shell said the result reflected strong operational performance in a volatile commodity environment. Its Products business delivered record results from refining, while refinery utilisation exceeded 100 percent when Rheinland was excluded because low Rhine water levels affected the site.

The company announced a further 5 billion US dollar share buyback programme, which it expects to complete by the release of its fourth-quarter results. Shell's distribution policy remains 40 to 50 percent of cash flow from operations through the cycle. Management also said the progressive dividend remains a key priority, with dividend per share up 9 percent over the previous 12 months.

The capital-return decision came alongside portfolio changes. Shell completed the acquisition of ARC Resources in September, strengthening its Canadian natural gas position and adding 370,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day of production. The company also took the final investment decision on the second phase of LNG Canada, which is expected to double liquefaction capacity at the facility and add nearly 6 million tonnes of annual LNG volumes for Shell.

Shell set its 2026 cash capital expenditure range at 23 billion to 25 billion US dollars, including about 4 billion US dollars for the ARC Resources acquisition. Management said net debt had fallen by 6 billion US dollars since the end of 2025, while gearing stood at 17 percent at the end of the third quarter, or below 3 percent excluding leases.
Shell stock traded at 46.52 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:46 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Shell stock.

Shell's operating performance and larger buyback improve the near-term capital-return profile, but refining conditions and energy-market volatility remain important variables for future earnings. The planned increase in LNG capacity and the ARC acquisition provide longer-term growth support, while the unusually strong refining contribution sets a demanding comparison for subsequent quarters.

Shell stock draws focus after record Q3 refining margins
sum: Shell reported strong third-quarter results on Thursday, October 29, as record refining margins and firmer gas-related performance lifted profitability. The company said its adjusted earnings reached 10.81 billion US dollars, nearly twice the 5.43 billion US dollars recorded a year earlier. CNBC reported that the result exceeded an LSEG-compiled analyst expectation of 9.92 billion US dollars and represented Shell's strongest adjusted profit since the second quarter of 2022.

Shell's global indicative refining margin reached 42 US dollars per barrel in the quarter, compared with 24 US dollars in the second quarter and 28.04 US dollars at the previous record cited by CNBC. The margin surge supported the Chemicals and Products division, while higher realised liquefied natural gas prices and stronger Integrated Gas volumes also contributed.

Shell's investor release said adjusted earnings were helped by higher refining margins, higher realised LNG prices and increased Integrated Gas volumes. Lower crude and oil products trading, higher well write-offs and lower realised liquids prices partly offset those gains. The company also reported 21 billion US dollars in cash flow from operations for the quarter.

Shell announced a new 5 billion US dollar share buyback programme, which it expects to complete by the announcement of its fourth-quarter 2026 results. The programme is larger than the 3 billion US dollar buyback cited by CNBC for the previous quarter. Shell said the new plan follows completion of the earlier repurchases.

Chief Executive Wael Sawan said Shell delivered strong operational performance amid continued severe disruption to the global energy system. For investors, the earnings beat and expanded repurchase programme strengthen the near-term shareholder-return profile, but they also leave results sensitive to refining spreads, LNG realisations, trading conditions and geopolitical supply disruptions.
The real-time quote of Shell stock was 47.30 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 12:00 CET on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
Shell's next major scheduled catalyst is the fourth-quarter 2026 results announcement, when the company expects to report progress on the buyback programme.

Here’s the dividend forecast for Shell shares in 2027 and 2028
sum: Can Shell (LSE:SHEL) shares keep growing their dividend through 2027 and 2028 while oil prices remain unpredictable? For UK income investors, the question matters.
The oil major is a FTSE 100 heavyweight, yet its dividend is declared in US dollars. That adds an extra angle to any dividend forecast, as the pounds received can move with the exchange rate.

Shell's board aims to increase the dividend per share by around 4% every year, subject to approval. That's a progressive policy rather than a fixed pledge, but it gives investors a clear starting point.

The company also targets total shareholder distributions of 40%–50% of cash flow from operations through the cycle. That includes both dividends and buybacks, working together to boost value through share count reduction and attractive payouts.
The latest Q3 quarterly dividend announced on 29 October 2026 was set at 39c per share. So that's our baseline for any 2027 and 2028 estimate.

If Shell follows its stated 4% growth aim, the annual dividend could rise from an estimated 155.9c per share in 2026 to about 163.1c in 2027. Most of the analysis I've reviewed expects a yield of roughly 3.11% at that level.

The sterling amount isn't fixed yet. Shell announces dollar dividends first, then sets the pound and euro equivalents closer to payment. UK shareholders normally receive sterling unless they elect another currency.

sum: Shell (ISIN GB00BP6MXD84) is due to report third-quarter results on October 29, 2026, with analysts forecasting USD 93.25 billion in revenue, according to MarketBeat. Shell stock was at EUR 48.12 at Lang & Schwarz on October 23, 2026 at 4:31 p.m. CEST.

The upcoming report will give investors a fresh view of Shell's operating performance after a strong second quarter. MarketBeat said Shell reported USD 3.52 in earnings per share and USD 94.66 billion in revenue for the previous quarter, against consensus estimates of USD 3.23 and USD 86.22 billion, respectively.

The revenue comparison represented a USD 8.44 billion beat versus consensus in the second quarter of 2026. The earnings-per-share difference was USD 0.29. Those figures provide the clearest benchmark for the October report, while the USD 93.25 billion forecast points to a lower sequential revenue figure than the second-quarter result.

Shell's NYSE-listed American depositary share was quoted at USD 108.00 on October 23, 2026 at 2:35 p.m. UTC, with a 52-week range of USD 68.62 to USD 108.08 and a market capitalization of USD 307.2 billion. The price-to-earnings ratio was 11.90 and the trailing dividend yield was 3.00 percent. The same quote showed a volume of 1,174,670 shares.

Shell's London listing remains the relevant home-market reference for British investors, while the euro quotation gives German investors a direct intraday indication. The October 29 report is the next major company date identified in the current coverage.

The forecast matters because it will be measured against both the USD 94.66 billion second-quarter result and the USD 86.22 billion consensus estimate that Shell exceeded. A result near USD 93.25 billion would therefore show whether the second-quarter revenue advantage persisted into the third quarter.

Shell combines a scheduled earnings catalyst with a EUR 48.12 Lang & Schwarz quotation on October 23, 2026 at 4:31 p.m. CEST. Why Shell Shares Have Jumped on Tuesday
sum: Shares in Shell plc (LON: SHEL) rose on Tuesday after the energy major issued a second-quarter 2026 update note flagging stronger-than-expected refining margins, robust gas trading and improved cash flow, even as Middle East tensions continue to disrupt Qatari gas output.

Shell stock climbed as much as 2.6% to around 2,989p in London trading, up from Monday’s close of 2,912.5p, as investors welcomed signs that the group’s downstream and trading businesses are offsetting geopolitical headwinds upstream.

The update, released ahead of full results on July 30, showed the company’s Chemicals and Products division benefiting from a sharp rise in margins: indicative refining margins are expected to jump to around $20 per barrel, up from $17/bbl in the first quarter, while indicative chemicals margins are forecast to roughly triple to about $240 per tonne, from $139/tonne previously. Refinery utilisation is also expected to hit close to 100%.

Shell’s Integrated Gas division highlighted that Trading & Optimisation results are expected to be “significantly higher” than in the first quarter, helping cushion the blow from lower Qatari LNG volumes. The company cut its Q2 gas production guidance to 610,000-650,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, down from 909,000 in Q1, directly citing the impact of the ongoing Middle East conflict on operations in Qatar.

Elsewhere, working capital movements are expected to swing to a positive $1-6 billion range, a marked improvement from the $11.2 billion outflow in Q1, reflecting recent volatility in commodity prices. Upstream production guidance was broadly maintained at 1.75-1.85 million boe/d.

Analysts said the combination of stronger margins and trading gains appears sufficient to offset the Qatar-related production hit, supporting sentiment ahead of full results and consensus estimates due July 22.
